align.prompt: Run the llm-straighten LLM ablation baseline for as-twn-taichung (variant orig), maximising H/V under the hard rules, then chain on the LLM network loop.

transcript.note: Taichung is a single unbranched path 0-4-3-2-1 sitting on a perfect NE diagonal (0,0)(1,1)(2,2)(3,3)(4,4), so hv=0 while hvd=4 — every segment is 45 degrees and none is H/V. Principle: a 4-segment path can reach hv=4/4 by turning the diagonal into a monotone staircase that alternates V,H,V,H, and that is the maximum the alignment score can reach, so I aim straight at it instead of upgrading segments one at a time. Choice of staircase phase: I anchor the south-west terminal 0 at (0,0) and pull each of the other four vertices onto the axis of its predecessor, alternating which axis I collapse (4 onto 0's column, 3 onto 4's row, 2 onto 3's column, 1 onto 2's row). That keeps the whole chain monotone in both axes, i.e. the SW-to-NE geographic trend of the Green Line survives, and every displacement is 1-2 cells, which is far cheaper in drift than the other hv=4 solution (collapsing all five vertices into one column, which would cost 10 cells of displacement for exactly the same score). Hard rules: quadrant rule allows landing exactly on a neighbour's row/col (sign 0 is free), which is what every one of these moves does; the path stays x- and y-monotone so no segment can swallow a vertex or cross another; all vertices are degree <=2 so the winding-order rule is not even evaluated.
